subject: Clarify custody & telemetry export limits for LLM pilot
messages:
From: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@sunrisehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@sunrisehealth.com>, Sunrise Health Contracts <contracts@sunrisehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot question: telemetry & derivative licensing

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the DPA draft and had a couple of questions before we circulate to procurement. Two items came up that we want to confirm for the pilot:

1) Telemetry exports: will any aggregated telemetry (latency, token usage, model selection) be shareable for our internal analytics? We need clarity on whether telemetry data is considered "customer data" vs. operational metadata.

2) Derivative licensing: the DPA language currently ties back to "no model training without consent" but doesn't say whether generated responses that include de-identified patient-like examples would be treated as redistributable. For our contract we need a clean statement that customer outputs from the pilot remain Customer IP and are not used for model improvement.

Can you confirm both items or point us to the operational steps you would provide as proof (logs, attestation, onshore routing)? If you can share a short implementation matrix (who does what, where data lives, evidence we can request) that would be helpful for our SOC/privacy review.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants to start paperwork next week.

Best,
Sally Nguyen
Sr. Contracts Manager
Sunrise Health

Attachments: Sunrise_DPA_comments_v1.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot question: telemetry & derivative licensing

On Fri, Nov 14, 2025 at 09:12 AM Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@sunrisehealth.com> wrote:
> Marcus —
> 
> Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the DPA draft and had a couple of questions before we circulate to procurement. Two items came up that we want to confirm for the pilot:
> 
> 1) Telemetry exports: will any aggregated telemetry (latency, token usage, model selection) be shareable for our internal analytics? We need clarity on whether telemetry data is considered "customer data" vs. operational metadata.
> 
> 2) Derivative licensing: the DPA language currently ties back to "no model training without consent" but doesn't say whether generated responses that include de-identified patient-like examples would be treated as redistributable. For our contract we need a clean statement that customer outputs from the pilot remain Customer IP and are not used for model improvement.
> 
> Can you confirm both items or point us to the operational steps you would provide as proof (logs, attestation, onshore routing)? If you can share a short implementation matrix (who does what, where data lives, evidence we can request) that would be helpful for our SOC/privacy review.
> 
> Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants to start paperwork next week.

Sally — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front:

- Telemetry: we consider low-level operational telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts) as operational metadata, not customer content. For the pilot we can provide an aggregated telemetry export (CSV) scoped to your tenant and filtered to omit any prompt/response content. We can also produce a signed attestation describing what fields are included.

- Derivative licensing / outputs: Redwood will commit to a pilot-level no-model-improvement clause: outputs produced by your tenant in the pilot will not be used to update any production models or training corpora without explicit written consent. We can add language to the DPA and supply an ops checklist showing where we enforce the flag (no-learn routing + segregated cache).

I've looped in Kimberly and David to provide the ops matrix and a proposed evidence pack (what we can hand you: exported telemetry, KV cache snapshots for retention proof, and access logs with redactions). Kimberly, David — can you attach the matrix and point to the DocuSign path when ready?

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood provides redlined DPA with a short paragraph for "no-model-improvement for pilot" and telemetry definition.
- Ops delivers an implementation matrix and evidence checklist in one business day.
- Procurement signs pilot SOW; proof artifacts delivered as part of onboarding.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call if teams want to walk through the matrix.

—Marcus Lin
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-ops-matrix.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@sunrisehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot question: telemetry & derivative licensing — implementation matrix

Marcus / Sally —

Following Marcus's note, attaching the implementation matrix and a short ops runbook. In brief:

- Telemetry export: we will provide a tenant-scoped CSV containing aggregated metrics (per-minute token counts, avg latency, model_id). No prompt/response content will be included. Fields: timestamp, model_id (hash), request_count, avg_latency_ms, error_rate. We will sign the CSV and include a checksum for verification.

- Onshore routing / residency: for the pilot we can route all inference to our US-dedicated pool (region: us-west1). Data at rest for the telemetry CSV and access logs will be retained in the US region.

- No-model-improvement enforcement: requests from your tenant will be tagged at the ingress level with no_learn=true; downstream training pipelines discard any traffic with that tag. We will provide an attestation and a snapshot of KV cache retention settings within 3 business days after onboarding.

- Evidence we can provide on request: signed telemetry CSV, redacted access logs (request ids + timestamps), ops attestation PDF, and a short video walkthrough of the routing configuration. The attached matrix maps each evidence artifact to the contractual language your team requested.

Links:
- Drive (matrix & runbook): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwoodPilot
- DocuSign (DPA + SOW): https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/Start?envelopeId=AA123456

Kimberly (ops) will be the primary contact for evidence delivery; David will own the attestation and the cache snapshot.

Kimberly Park
Principal, Privacy & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-ops-matrix.xlsx

From: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@sunrisehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sunrise Health Contracts <contracts@sunrisehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@sunrisehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot question: telemetry & derivative licensing — implementation matrix

Thanks — this is very helpful and aligns with what legal needs. A few quick items before we finalize:

1) Please add a one-line DPA clause we can paste into our negotiating redline that states: "Provider shall not use Customer prompts, responses, or derived outputs for model training or improvement, and Customer outputs shall be retained as Customer IP for the duration of the agreement."

2) Procurement needs the DocuSign envelope opened by Friday so we can get PO approval. Marcus / Kimberly — can you confirm the envelope will include the DPA amendment + 90-day pilot SOW?

If those two items are in place we will move forward and procurement will initiate the PO. I will share the Sunrise redline once we get the DPA clause inserted.

Best,
Sally
Sr. Contracts Manager
Sunrise Health
